newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal bank chief says inflation goal possible.
newsitem.headline: Portugal bank chief says inflation goal possible.

text.p: The governor of the Bank of Portugal said on Wednesday that Portugal could get inflation down to a goal of 2.25-2.50 percent next year, despite a European Commission forecast for 3.0 percent.
"The position of the Bank is that the target presented by the government is perfectly credible, assuming exchange rate stability and salary restraint," Antonio de Sousa told journalists.

The European Commission forecast on Wednesday that Portugal's inflation rate, as measured by a rolling 12-month average, would stand at 3.0 percent at the end of 1997, down from 3.3 percent this year.
